question.problem: Expressed as a nonnegative integer smaller than $11,$ the additive inverse of $22$ modulo $11$ is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
The additive inverse of $22$ modulo $11$ is the integer $0\le x<11$ such that

$$
x+22≡0\,(\text{mod}\,11).
$$

First, note that $22≡2\cdot 11≡0\,(\text{mod}\,11),$ and $0+0≡0\,(\text{mod}\,11).$

Therefore, the additive inverse of the element $22$ modulo $11$ is $0.$

We can verify this result as follows:

$$
22+0≡2\cdot 11+0≡2\cdot 0+0≡0\,\,✓\,(\text{mod}\,11)
$$

**Note:** In general, the additive inverse of $a$ modulo $n$ is simply the residue of $-a$ modulo $n,$ i.e. $-a\,\text{mod}\,n.$
